title: Virtual networks: NAT, bridge and isolated internal network

videos.script: A guest's network card is plugged into a switch that only exists on the host. What that switch is connected to decides everything about the guest's network. {{switch}} There are three common answers. NAT: the guest hides behind the host and borrows its address. Bridged: the guest stands on the real network beside the host, like one more computer. Isolated: the guest shares a room with the host and nobody else. {{three}} Every hypervisor offers the same three, under different names, and knowing which is which answers most network complaints about a guest before you open a single setting. {{names}} You will build all three and watch each from the other side. A printer on a small office network keeps a list of who came to see it. {{printer}}
